variantOf: public/models/yggdrasil.glb (same generator seed, skeleton and scale, so the two line up if swapped or cross-faded)
concept: A world tree woven from glowing filaments with a cosmic leaf crown inspired by Loki's Yggdrasil: the crown is luminous haze rather than solid foliage - deep indigo, violet and dark purple, glowing electric-violet nebula cores against darker pockets, soft translucent edges and star-like glints. Dense twisting bundles run through the trunk and roots, threads split into every limb and branch (branches 40% denser than the base build); every branch thread, twig and light-wisp stays inside the leaf crown. Strands keep the Hyperiux orange heat ramp.

generatorScripts: blender/yggdrasil/scripts/ygg_build.py (skeleton, leaf cards incl. build_geometry(seed, leaf_density, leaf_scale), leaf material)

blender/yggdrasil/scripts/ygg_strands.py (filaments; branch_density=1.4; leaf_density=2.0; leaf_scale=1.35; build(..., leaves="cosmic" | "green" | "amber" | None); with leaves, clip_to_leaves keeps branch threads, twigs and wisps inside the leaf crown; cosmic_hue() picks each leaf card's hue from smooth noise + height; set_cosmic_preview() swaps in a Blender-only material that matches the three.js setup)
blender/yggdrasil/scripts/ygg_stage_export.py (night preview stage with leaf_fill moon + trunk-glow lights, bloom, export)
previews: blender/yggdrasil/yggdrasil-strands-preview.png (cosmic leaves, rendered at leaf colour x1.7 with the leaves covering the inner strands, as in three.js)
source.determinism: the generator uses noise.noise() only (mathutils.noise.noise_vector changes per Blender launch), so the same seed rebuilds the identical tree in any session; the realistic yggdrasil.glb was re-exported from the same skeleton so both variants line up
source.textures: blender/yggdrasil/textures/leaf_cosmic_atlas.png (1024 RGBA, baked from leaf_atlas.png: each of the 4 atlas cells recoloured to one hue - indigo, violet, deep purple, electric violet - through a steep space-black -> hue -> glow ramp on the leaf luminance, with per-hue brightness tiers; alpha is softened and scaled by brightness so dark parts are thin haze; ~110 star glints per cell)
source.previewLighting: the cosmic leaves are unlit, so the preview needs no scene lights; bloom only

orientation.origin: trunk centre on the ground plane (y = 0)

dimensions.heightNote: same skeleton and scale as yggdrasil.glb; the 35% bigger leaf cards reach 40.3 m at the crown top and widen the crown by under 1 m

YGG_StrandRoots.content: filaments through every root, twisted companion root and rootlet; dim toward the root tips

YGG_StrandTrunk.content: dense twisting bundle through the trunk core and the 7 braided trunk strands (the strands that continue into the limbs carry the denser branch thread count)

YGG_StrandBranches.content: threads splitting into the 7 limbs, the leader and every level-1 and level-2 branch (1.4x the base thread count, at least 4 threads per branch), plus twig-threads that peel off along branches and roots; branch threads and twigs end inside the leaf crown

YGG_StrandCanopy.content: light-wisps fanning out of branch tips and through the foliage pads, shortened where needed so each fades to black inside the leaf crown

YGG_StrandLeaves.content: cosmic leaf sprays on the realistic tree's foliage pads: twice the realistic tree's cards (the same base cards plus one extra card per base card, per pad) and every spray card 35% bigger, so the crown reads as a full nebula mass. Each card samples one hue cell of the cosmic atlas, picked from its centre, so hues form nebula patches: electric-violet glowing cores, violet body, deep purple pockets, dark indigo outer/lower crown

attributes._phase: per-pad random phase for desynchronised wind
attributes._flow: 0.88-1.0, top of the strand flow (for an optional pulse)

filaments.geometry: core strands are 3-sided tubes (5-10 cm radius); fine threads, twigs and wisps are twisting ribbons (2-6 cm wide) that never sit fully edge-on

vertexData.COLOR_0: linear RGB = Hyperiux orange heat ramp (deep red-orange -> brand orange #FF5C0D-ish -> hot amber near the trunk) x brightness (fades toward root tips and wisp tips)
vertexData.uv: u = across the strand (0..1); v = the same flow coordinate as _flow
vertexData._flow: 0 at the root tips -> 0.5 at the trunk base -> 1 at the canopy wisp tips. three.js attribute name: _flow
vertexData._seed: random 0..1 per filament, to desynchronise pulses / flicker. three.js attribute name: _seed

material.YGG_Strand: KHR_materials_unlit (three.js MeshBasicMaterial, vertexColors = true), double-sided, no textures.
material.YGG_CosmicLeaves: KHR_materials_unlit (three.js MeshBasicMaterial), cosmic atlas base colour + soft alpha (alphaMode BLEND), double-sided, no normals. Self-luminous: needs no scene light.

threeJsSetup.material: strands (YGG_Strand, no map): material.blending = THREE.AdditiveBlending; material.depthWrite = false; material.transparent = true; material.color.setScalar(0.18); mesh.renderOrder = 0. Leaves (YGG_CosmicLeaves, has a map): keep the loaded NormalBlending + transparent; material.depthWrite = false (soft haze cards must not hide each other); material.color.setScalar(1.7) so the glowing cores reach the bloom (1.3 = darker and moodier, 2.4 = brighter violet); mesh.renderOrder = 2 so the leaf haze draws over the strands and the crown reads as a full nebula mass (renderOrder below the strands instead shows every branch thread through the crown).
threeJsSetup.bloom: UnrealBloomPass(strength 0.65, radius 0.4, threshold 0.6) with ACESFilmic tone mapping on a dark background
threeJsSetup.why: thousands of strands overlap in the trunk and root flare; with additive blending a colour gain above ~0.25 saturates the base to white
threeJsSetup.flowPulse: in onBeforeCompile pass _flow and _seed as varyings, then e.g. band = fract(vFlow * 3.0 - uTime * 0.25 + vSeed * 0.15); outgoingLight *= 0.75 + 2.2 * smoothstep(0.0, 0.06, band) * (1.0 - smoothstep(0.06, 0.22, band)); this sends bright pulses from the root tips up through the trunk into the canopy
threeJsSetup.verified: loaded and rendered with three r186 GLTFLoader + DRACOLoader + UnrealBloomPass (strands gain 0.18, bloom 0.65/0.4/0.6, leaves x1.7, depthWrite false, leaves renderOrder 2); leaves load as MeshBasicMaterial transparent; no errors
threeJsSetup.lighting: none required: strands and cosmic leaves are both unlit. Scene lights do not affect this asset.
threeJsSetup.whyNotAdditiveLeaves: tried: additive leaves wash out to pale lavender where the crown is dense and let the orange strands swamp the crown

budget.glbBytes: about 8.9 MB (Draco geometry + 1024 cosmic leaf atlas PNG; no normal map)
